speakers: Graham Robertson (partner, head of client portfolio management, Man AHL)
summary: Graham Robertson (Man AHL) reviews H1 2024 trend following and argues trend delivers equity-like returns with zero correlation, strongest in sustained sell-offs and as a partial bond substitute. AHL's approach is maximum diversification across many price drivers (especially alternative markets), a constant volatility target and uncapped equity exposure; AI has not revolutionised the strategy.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: q1 one very strong as you hinted I would say Q2 has been much more about consolidation
claims.claim: In H1 2024 trend following had a strong Q1 and consolidated in Q2, with long stocks and credit working and fixed income range-bound and harder to trade.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Trend following in general has been cutting his positions as as that that that that Coco position has got bigger
claims.claim: Volatility-scaled trend followers cut a market's position as its volatility rises, so they were not driving the cocoa surge even while it was a key winner.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: if you're not slightly uncomfortable with a position you're probably not making money
claims.claim: Profitable trend positions (e.g. short bonds in 2022, SVB 2023) are uncomfortable, and the short fixed income position looked vulnerable as prices rallied in mid-2024.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: lots of emotion involved in prices and that's something I think Trend following as a strategy can really take advantage of
claims.claim: Crypto (Bitcoin and Ether futures) trended strongly in 2024 because emotion-driven prices suit trend following.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: we think the more you diversify the the better
claims.claim: The more asset classes and markets in a trend portfolio the better; crypto and China are offered as separate vehicles because some investors object to them in the core portfolio.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you've got an asset class or a style of trading which is performed as well as equities in the long term completely diversifying to it
claims.claim: Trend following has returned about as much as equities over the long run with near-zero correlation, and does well when equities do badly.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the short bonds position was profitable and the Long Dollar positions were were profitable too
claims.claim: In April 2024 equities fell but trend followers still gained because short bonds and long dollar paid, so trend performance cannot be read from equities alone.
claims.indicator: trend positioning in bonds, FX, equities

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's kind of the one part of your portfolio where investors really should have no opinion
claims.claim: Investors should hold no view on a trend allocation, as transparency invites opinions that are rarely useful.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: things like us Japanese equities are doing well we have some currencies like the Yen maybe the aid dollar also contributing
claims.claim: Trend resurged in July 2024 through US and Japanese equities, yen and AUD, softs (coffee instead of cocoa), grains and metals, after a soft Q2.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I see a lot of small losses a lot of markets providing small losses
claims.claim: 2024 is a classical trend year: many small losses and a handful of markets drive most performance, even in a 100-market portfolio.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: pulling the trigger going short bonds after such a long bull market run is very difficult
claims.claim: Most trend followers went short bonds around Q4 2021; discretionary macro managers who were bearish hesitated and used rate-sensitive proxies that did worse; at 5% rates low-vol CTAs were sold for bonds.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: a much more attractive proposition than than bonds at 1% the yield
claims.claim: With yields at 5% bonds are far more attractive than at 1%, and trend's short bond position is fading after 2022.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: 2022 was a year where I think US Treasury had their worst year in about 200
claims.claim: Bonds failed as an equity hedge in 2022 (worst year in about 200) while trend gained, so trend can substitute part of a bond allocation.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: perhaps it's something you should have even if you don't want to you know get rid of your Bond's position maybe substitute some of that Bond position for a a trend falling position
claims.claim: Investors increasingly consider trend alongside or in place of part of a bond allocation, as bonds no longer reliably rally when equities sell off.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: btp 50 up 1.23% for the month up 8.41% so far this year
claims.claim: Mid-July 2024: BTOP50 +8.4%, SG CTA +8.3%, SG Trend +10.4%, short-term traders +1.3% YTD; MSCI World +14%, S&P 500 +19%.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the Futures Trend following historically at least has had a a slightly lower sharp of the order of5 six something like that
claims.claim: Futures trend following has a Sharpe of roughly 0.5-0.6 but works particularly well in crises.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the alternative markets tends to perform more steady over time maybe 8.9 sharp something like that um and doesn't have the same kind of Crisis Alpha
claims.claim: Alternative (OTC, harder-to-access) markets have higher, steadier Sharpe (about 0.8-0.9) but no crisis alpha.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the key driver for that market is weather patterns
claims.claim: Liquid futures are tied to the macroeconomy so crises show up in them, while alternative markets like Nord Pool power have independent drivers, hence no crisis alpha; combine both for maximum diversification.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: perhaps people have realized that oh if there CTA portfolio is doing well they actually have to lighten up a bit in order to rebalance back
claims.claim: CTA flows are hard to predict because after strong CTA years multi-asset investors rebalance out, so interest does not follow performance.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: to me trend is its own timing mechanism
claims.claim: Trend follows its own direction changes, so timing an allocation to trend is very hard; large institutions hold it, wealth clients try to time it.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: an environment where inflation has picked up looking at CPI globally and fallen
claims.claim: Inflation rising and falling moves markets, as before 1970, which suits trend following.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you tend to get those kind of pain points for Trend followers reversals in markets during strongly trending periods
claims.claim: Trend's worst weeks (reversals such as the SVB flight to quality) occur during strongly trending periods and the 12 months before and after are relatively good.
claims.indicator: worst weekly returns of SG Trend
claims.testable: yes - event study of worst weeks (done on SG Trend)

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you can really deal with whatever level of risk that people want to take we typically Target risk levels not necess returns
claims.claim: Trend portfolios target risk levels, so volatility (low, or 10-15%) is chosen by investor preference.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you start taking out things like Commodities of a portfolio it actually is not uh beneficial to you from an investing point of view
claims.claim: ESG exclusions of commodities cut low-correlation return sources, a tradeoff between returns and policy.
claims.testable: yes - backtest with and without commodities

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: from our experience people probably didn't had have enough that was really our our key point
claims.claim: Allocations under 2% do not move the needle; the right trend weight depends on the metric (Sharpe, drawdown) and portfolio vol (7-8% BTOP vs 12-14% SG Trend), but most hold too little.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the tracking error that Trend following tends to have is exaggerated most when it's performing well
claims.claim: Trend's tracking error is largest when risk assets do badly, so its different line item works in the right direction.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: some of our colleagues who have embraced say um putting Trend with say long equities and created these combined products with a lot of success
claims.claim: Packaging trend with long equities (return stacking) hides the standalone line-item problem and sells well, avoiding the word trend.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Trend by definition is is vulnerable at reversal points
claims.claim: Trend is vulnerable at macro reversals, so diversify with similar yield-put strategies such as long-short quality, which handles flight-to-quality episodes like SVB.
claims.testable: yes - test quality vs trend in reversals

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: it's the thing that causes pain on a monthly basis
claims.claim: Like insurance, trend causes monthly pain, but should be held all the time because the need for it cannot be timed.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: every Market has the ability to Trend and the key to obtaining performance is to diversify across as many different price drivers as you can
claims.claim: AHL's research: every market can trend, so diversify across many distinct price drivers rather than correlated contracts.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you build a portfolio which is a target volatility in the long term according to your simulation and you fluctuate a little bit above that
claims.claim: Portfolios target a fairly constant long-run volatility, a little above in trending environments and below when trends are scarce, unchanged over 13 years.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: there's a flaw in that argument and that if L was to zero you can have an infinite position
claims.claim: Volatility scaling needs a safeguard because as volatility approaches zero the position size goes to infinity.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the real determinant of performance has been diversifying diversification identifying lots and lots of different markets
claims.claim: Over the last 13 years the main determinant of performance has been diversification via many markets, especially alternative markets.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: we found that diversifying alternative markets performed well in that period in a way that traditional Futures markets were were
claims.claim: In the post-GFC 'CTA winter' (central bank intervention, Fed put), alternative markets did well while traditional futures struggled.
claims.indicator: alternative-market trend vs SG Trend / BTOP50

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: in years where there were strong Trends concentrated portfolio uh was able to profit really strongly from that but it was the diversification that really helped you out in the years that were a little bit more tricky
claims.claim: A Quantica simulation framework showed diversified portfolios pay off most in years when trend following struggles, while concentrated ones win in strong-trend years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: by trading fewer markets have a more meaningful exposure to them that in itself can also make a huge difference
claims.claim: A few managers trading few markets did very well in 2022-24 by holding larger exposure to the big movers, but this makes manager selection harder.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the huge variation in performance you get with markets holding periods risk weight continues to fascinate me
claims.claim: Trend managers' performance varies greatly with markets, holding periods and risk weights even though the concept is the same.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: clearly not a parent a pattern that's been seen or could be in any training set
claims.claim: ML/AI pattern recognition fails in unprecedented events (Covid), so AI-based trend systems did not preserve crisis alpha or zero correlation; AI has not revolutionised trend following yet.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: it's very good for lots of things you know if you want to load up a research document ask it questions
claims.claim: LLMs help with research documents, code and NLP on balance sheets, but outputs can hallucinate and need checking.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: S&P 500 correlation which just hit the highest level in like 27 years
claims.claim: The 1-year rolling correlation of the 10-year Treasury with the S&P 500 hit its highest in 27 years, weakening bonds as diversifier.
claims.indicator: rolling stock-bond correlation (10y note vs S&P 500)

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: what we've always said about Trend flowing is that this crisis Alpha property tends to hold for sustained sell-offs
claims.claim: Trend's crisis alpha holds for sustained sell-offs, not for sudden equity drops where the result depends on positioning; bonds rally on sudden drops.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you really do limit your long-term return potential if you cap that equities exposure
claims.claim: Capping long-equity exposure in a trend program cuts long-term returns (as seen in 2016 research and Quantica Q2); in 2017, one big long-equity trend, capped trend lagged by 10-20%.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if people think they have too many equities they should sell the equities
claims.claim: Reducing equity exposure is better done in the equity portfolio than by capping equities inside trend following.
